rubric.statement: Each invocation of the function returned by `asyncify` copies the caller's current `thread_local_overrides`, so DSPy configuration is captured at call time rather than only when the wrapper is created.
The worker-side wrapper merges the captured overrides onto the worker thread's existing overrides for the `program(*a, **kw)` call and resets the prior override state in a `finally` block afterward.

`asyncify` executes the program by awaiting an `asyncer.asyncify(wrapped_program, ...)` callable, matching the source's worker-thread wrapper model instead of running the program inline in the async function body.

Concurrency is gated by the `CapacityLimiter` returned by `get_limiter()`, and `get_limiter()` keeps a module-level singleton limiter whose `total_tokens` is updated to match `dspy.settings.async_max_workers` instead of constructing a new limiter each time.

Tests pin the default limiter size at 8, require the same limiter object to be reused across `async_max_workers` changes, and check that elapsed time scales with `number_of_tasks / capacity` when many asyncified calls are awaited together.
